info.title: GuraDB M0 HTTP read-only SQL
info.description: M0 single-process SELECT over pinned Parquet manifests. Only int8/text/bool, one registered table, column projection/filter/order/constant LIMIT. No writes, joins, functions or transactions. PostgreSQL wire is a separately configured bounded loopback interface; this OpenAPI describes HTTP only. See docs/design/m0-parquet-http.md for hard caps and certified scope; this is not a distributed or release-ready database.

servers.description: Reserved illustrative hostname; not a deployed service.

post.summary: Submit one parameterized read-only SQL statement
post.description: Acceptance does not indicate query success. This endpoint rejects DDL, DML and side-effecting statements before execution. Tenant and principal are derived from authenticated identity. Batch writes and synchronization are outside this contract.

example.sql: SELECT asset_id, media_type FROM assets WHERE media_type = $1 ORDER BY asset_id LIMIT 10

202.description: Accepted query handle; poll status for final outcome.

get.description: Status failures are structured on QueryHandle.error. Terminal handles/results expire after operator-configured TTL (default/hard cap 60 seconds); known owned expiry=410, evicted tombstones/unknown/restart/cross-subject=404. Current authorization required on every access.

200.description: Current status; a successful HTTP request does not imply a successful query.

delete.description: Cancellation races with completion; cancel_requested is not terminal. Once terminal, status never changes. Repeated calls return the current authorized handle without reverting a completed task to cancel_requested.

202.description: Cancellation requested or pending; poll for terminal state.

200.description: Query already terminal; existing outcome is unchanged.

get.summary: Read one page from a successful query result
get.description: Only available after status=succeeded. Results are bounded by total max_rows and response byte policy. Every data page carries the same read_context as its successful handle. Opaque cursors bind the fixed result snapshot, tenant and authorized principal, expire, and do not reexecute SQL. Non-ready=409; expired=410; inaccessible resources may use 404 to avoid disclosure.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque cursor from the previous page. Omit for the first page.

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description: Page size 1..1000, default 100; fixed result cap is separate.

200.description: A page from the fixed query result.

bearerAuth.description: M0 operator-managed SHA-256 Bearer allowlist, binding tenant/principal/datasets; reloads every request, fails closed. Use protected transport/trusted network; no OIDC/TLS server.

QueryId.name: query_id
QueryId.description: Opaque query handle, scoped and authorized by server identity.

RequestError.description: Request-level error: invalid request (400), unauthenticated (401), forbidden (403), not found (404), not ready (409), expired (410), over budget (429), or server failure (5xx). Execution failures after acceptance are reported on QueryHandle.error.

QueryRequest.description: M0 accepts only the documented SELECT/type whitelist and published views. Unsupported syntax is rejected before object I/O. General PG compatibility remains planned.

sql.description: One supported read-only SQL statement; planning/execution must reject side effects. Parameters are bound separately, never interpolated.

parameters.description: Positional $1..$n. int8 safe JSON integer or typed canonical decimal string; text string; bool; null. Unknown and ambiguous types are rejected.

mode.description: Only read_only is accepted. The execution layer independently enforces side-effect freedom and principal permissions; this field cannot authorize writes.

timeout_ms.description: M0 default/hard cap; operator may reduce, request cannot exceed server cap.

max_rows.description: M0 default/hard cap; operator may reduce, request cannot exceed server cap.

read_consistency.description: published binds a complete published read view and may lag committed data. M0/M1 accept published only. data_committed is a later capability: bind an actual committed revision, compensate/scan correctly or wait within budget, otherwise fail. Reject unsupported modes rather than silently using published.

read_view_id.description: Pin an authorized published view covering every data resource in the query. Incompatible scope or expired sources must fail. Cannot combine with data_committed; current authorization still applies.

status.description: succeeded, failed and cancelled are terminal and immutable; a late cancellation request must not move them back to cancel_requested.

result_kind.description: Assigned by the server planner, never by the caller. data includes any query reading dataset contents, even aggregates or constant projections; metadata is restricted to constants and catalog-only queries without dataset reads.

type.description: M0 emits int8/text/bool. int8 values are decimal JSON strings; bool/text/null use native JSON values. Other SQL types are not implemented.

rows.description: Values follow columns. M0 int8 is always a decimal JSON string without precision loss; text/bool/null use native JSON. No other types supported.

next_cursor.description: Null means no further page in this bounded result set, not necessarily all source rows were returned.

truncated.description: True when total result row cap omitted rows. It is not a pagination indicator.

result_kind.description: Assigned by the server planner, never by the caller. data includes any query reading dataset contents, even aggregates or constant projections; metadata is restricted to constants and catalog-only queries without dataset reads.

retryable.description: Retry may be possible; a newly submitted query can read another version unless its view is pinned.

sqlstate.description: Present only where a PostgreSQL-compatible mapping is defined.

details.description: Sanitized structured context, excluding credentials and private query parameters.

version.description: Opaque source snapshot, dataset version or immutable manifest identity. Not a cross-source transaction timestamp.

ReadContext.description: Required for successful data handles and every data result page. The same fixed revision, sources and index set are retained across pages. Versions describe what was read, not a global atomic moment. Catalog-only/constant queries use result_kind=metadata and omit this object.

data_revision_id.description: Opaque aggregate revision binding every data source selected for this query; not an arbitrary single-table snapshot ID.

read_view_id.description: Opaque view binding the aggregate revision and its required index bundle. All result pages preserve this exact context.

QueryStats.description: Successful execution only. source_reads counts logical full-object reads, not SDK retries/HTTP wire requests. No source cache in M0; elapsed_ms excludes queue time.
